Fixes https://github.com/dotnet/runtime/issues/78953.

For usernames with Unicode characters we had a problem because Window's .cmd scripts are not supporting Unicode (https://ss64.com/nt/chcp.html). Temporary files paths, e.g. "C:\Users\煉\AppData\Local\Temp\tmpC538.tmp" were passed to emcc with incorrect encoding and then could not be found in the file system which caused exceptions.

### Out-of-scope:
- AOT tests for Unicode in the path
- publish with relink tests for Blazor are disabled because emscripten canot process unicode correctly when we run it here: https://github.com/dotnet/runtime/blob/99aa25fee09a3a66fb698720a234eb3d7770ca1a/src/mono/wasm/build/WasmApp.Native.targets#L475
https://github.com/emscripten-core/emscripten/issues/17817

lang:Eng(cnv:DeepL jp => en)
{
Create a local Windows account with a Japanese (Kanji, Hiragana, Katakana) account name (e.g. brick =utf-8"\u7149").
2. Install Visual Studio 2022 under that account, specifying a workload that can use ASP.NET Blazor WebAssembly.
Start Visual Studio 2022 and create a project with the non-empty Blazor WebAssembly template.
Build the project and confirm that no errors occur.
Publish the project to any folder.

The above steps fail to publish with an error message that the temporary files in the folder under the "Purgatory" folder of users are inaccessible. In addition, the displayed file path is garbled by mixing the "煉" character with the path splitting character.


Translated with www.DeepL.com/Translator (free version)

facing the exact same problem as @lensouko, different alphabet: Gaj's Latin. 

I just wanted to provide a quick workaround.  

- Open CMD as Administrator
- Navigate to "C:\Users"
- Execute the following command:  
   mklink /D "GARBLED USERNAME HERE" "NORMAL USERNAME HERE"
   (The command will create a directory symbolic link pointing from 'GARBLED' to your real username. )

   ex. mklink /D "Marko ┼áakic" "Marko Šakic"

- Dont close the CMD. Try to publish, It will probably fail again.
- Look for the new variant of the garbled username in the output window. 
- Execute mklink again with the new garbled username. 
- Try to publish. 

That should be it.
